label: rare: s/y/b/a input in w/o/v context (no clean rule)
explanation: Extremely sparse (0.014% of steps), weak activations (max 0.205). Fires in every phase except t=0,1, with about 60% of mass in the copy phase. Enriched when the input is s, y, b or a (78% of mass) and when the context contains w/o/c/v: out_tok w (13.8x lift), prev_tok o or v, prev2_tok c/w/o, first token w or c. The strongest examples are sequences that start with w w o. Still, every predicate tried has precision below 5% because the same tokens in the same contexts usually do not fire it, so it seems to be a specific hidden-state conjunction that the per-step variables do not capture. It never fires on incorrect copies and rarely on <DEL>. I did not find what controls its magnitude.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: in_tok=y (+4.12), in_tok=b (+3.90), phase=2 & in_tok=s (+3.89), prev_tok=o (+3.66), prev_tok=v (+3.60), phase=0 & in_tok=n (+3.33). Lower it: prev_tok=w (-2.36), to_go=6 (-1.33), in_first=0 (-1.10), n_digits=0 (-1.04).
